result.rationale: The diff clearly shows createAllCalendarEvents now falls back to `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: destination.credentialId } })` with no ownership scoping, whereas the previous code only used credentials from `this.calendarCredentials` (the booking context's own credentials). The same unscoped DB fetch is also added in updateEvent and handleCancelBooking. Whether the credentialId is attacker-controllable can't be verified from this diff alone, but the expansion of the credential lookup scope beyond the booking participants is directly visible and is a plausible security regression.

judged_text: createAllCalendarEvents resolves destination.credentialId via prisma.credential.findUnique on the raw primary key with no userId/teamId ownership scoping, replacing the previous lookup that was confined to the booking context's own credentials (this.calendarCredentials). A destinationCalendar row whose credentialId references a credential outside the booking participants (the destination-calendar settings write path takes credentialId from the client) now causes the victim's OAuth key to be fetched and used to create calendar events as that user; under the old code such a stored foreign credentialId was inert because the credential was never found in this.calendarCredentials.

adjudication.rationale: In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, when a `destination.credentialId` is present but not found in `this.calendarCredentials`, the new code falls back to `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: destination.credentialId } })` and then uses that credential to call `createEvent` (with `destination.externalId`). This DB lookup is scoped only by the raw primary key and does not verify ownership/association (e.g., `userId`/`teamId`) to the booking context/participants. Compared to the prior behavior (only using credentials present in `this.calendarCredentials`), this introduces the possibility that a stored/forged `destinationCalendar.credentialId` referencing an unrelated credential will be fetched and used.
